behavioral_effects: Chat turns skip the per-server MCP initialize+tools/list handshake when the last probe is younger than MCP_PROBE_TTL_SECS, removing the per-turn latency floor of the slowest configured server
A dead server stalls one turn for MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS, then is skipped from cache for MCP_PROBE_FAILURE_TTL_SECS instead of stalling every turn
compatibility_impact: None to any HTTP or WebSocket contract. Behavioural: a server that dies mid-TTL is attached for up to MCP_PROBE_TTL_SECS (300s default) and its tool calls fail visibly instead of the server being silently dropped; a recovered server reappears within MCP_PROBE_FAILURE_TTL_SECS (30s default). The connection test endpoint still probes uncached.
follow_up: If a dead-mid-TTL server failing a turn shows up in practice, catch the toolset-entry failure and invalidate that cache entry
limitations: The cache is per-process; multiple workers each probe once per window
Per-turn OAuth token refresh and DB connection listing in build_toolsets_for_user are untouched
reason: build_mcp_toolsets performs a full MCP initialize+tools/list handshake against every configured server on every chat turn; a healthy server re-proves liveness it demonstrated seconds ago and a dead one stalls every turn for MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS. A TTL cache keyed by server URL and auth-header hash skips redundant probes while the connection test endpoint keeps probing uncached
risks: A server that goes down mid-TTL is still attached for up to 300s; pydantic-ai entering that dead toolset at run start can fail the turn until the negative verdict replaces the stale positive one
rollback: git revert restores per-turn probing; the two new env vars are optional with defaults, so no deployment config change is needed either way
security_impact: None new. The cache key holds a SHA-256 fingerprint of the auth headers, never the headers or tokens, and distinct credentials against the same URL get distinct entries, so one user's auth failure cannot mark a server dead for others. The GitHub read-only assertion still evaluates every turn against the advertised tool list, and the per-call allowed_tools filter that actually blocks mutation tools is untouched. A stale reachable verdict grants no access: real credentials are presented on every tool call. SSRF validation of connection URLs is unchanged.
summary: Cache per-turn MCP liveness probe results with a TTL to cut chat-turn latency
